cards.name: statum
cards.summary: Typestate transitions and rehydration for persisted Rust workflows.
highlights: Moves invalid transitions into the type system instead of runtime guards
Rebuilds persisted machines into concrete typed states
Fits staged workflows where persistence and compile-time safety have to coexist

badge.text: Invalid transitions become impossible to write

code_examples.label: State machine
Transition

body.title: Transitions stay in the type system

features.text: Transition methods state both the starting and ending machine types.
The resulting API reads like workflow code instead of enum plumbing.

badge.text: Data moves with the state that owns it

code_examples.label: Data-bearing state
Transition with data

body.title: State-specific data stays attached to state-specific behavior

features.text: Review-only data appears only when the machine is actually in review.
The transition API makes data handoff explicit instead of leaking optional fields everywhere.

code_examples.label: Validator shape

body.title: Rehydration is part of the design, not an afterthought

features.text: Persistent rows validate into concrete machine states instead of generic runtime blobs.
Storage integration stays close to the workflow model instead of branching into a second untyped path.

cards.name: nestum
cards.summary: Nested enum construction and matching that preserves domain hierarchy.
highlights: Lets event and policy APIs read like the domain instead of wrapper plumbing
Preserves nested invariants without flattening everything into broad top-level variants
Keeps construction and matching syntax aligned across the same hierarchy

badge.text: Enum paths read like the actual domain hierarchy

code_examples.label: Definitions

features.text: The API keeps the conceptual tree visible at the call site.
Deeply modeled event trees stay readable without collapsing into flatter APIs.

badge.text: Pattern matching keeps the same nested vocabulary

code_examples.label: Match syntax

body.title: Matching keeps the same mental model as construction

features.text: The same nested path style works in both expression and pattern positions.
Intent survives in the noisiest parts of routing code.

badge.text: Hierarchies can stay intact across module boundaries

code_examples.label: External nesting

body.title: The hierarchy does not have to collapse at file boundaries

features.text: Cross-module nesting is opt-in and explicit.
The public path still reads as one coherent domain tree.

cards.name: modum
cards.summary: Workspace linting for namespace shape, naming, and API-surface rules.
highlights: Turns naming and namespace standards into a repeatable workspace check
Pushes API-shape review left instead of leaving it to one-off comments
Supports the same module-first standards used throughout this portfolio

badge.text: Readable paths become an enforceable rule

code_examples.label: Desired public shape

body.title: API shape is treated like a design constraint

features.text: The tool targets naming and namespace drift before it spreads across a workspace.
Code review can focus on behavior instead of recurring naming cleanup.

badge.text: Namespace-preserving imports are deliberate, not accidental

body.title: Imports can preserve the module vocabulary

features.text: Modules stay visible when they add context instead of just noise.
That makes call sites easier to scan in larger codebases.

badge.text: The standards run as tooling, not just prose

body.title: Style standards become part of the delivery loop

features.text: Policy can run across a whole workspace instead of being enforced ad hoc.
It turns naming standards into infrastructure rather than tribal knowledge.
